claim.quote: Here we present the first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions.

key_value_text.quote: We find that the integrated yields of strange and multi-strange particles relative to pions increases significantly with the event charged-particle multiplicity... In high-multiplicity events strangeness production reaches values similar to those observed in Pb-Pb collisions, where a QGP is formed.
key_value_text.value: Integrated yields of strange and multi-strange particles relative to pions increase significantly with event charged-particle multiplicity, reaching values similar to those seen in Pb-Pb collisions at the highest pp multiplicities.

name: First observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions

summary.plain: ALICE found that, in the busiest ordinary proton-proton collisions, unusual 'strange' particles are produced far more often than normal - a pattern previously seen only in collisions of heavy atomic nuclei and linked to the quark-gluon plasma.
summary.technical: ALICE measurement (pp at sqrt(s) = 7 TeV) of multi-strange hadron (K0s, Lambda, Xi, Omega) yields relative to pions as a function of charged-particle multiplicity: first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions, with yields at the highest multiplicities comparable to those in Pb-Pb collisions.

title: Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions
why_it_matters: Strangeness enhancement was long considered a signature of quark-gluon plasma formation in heavy-ion collisions specifically; finding it in ordinary proton-proton collisions at high multiplicity blurs the line between 'small' and 'large' collision systems and challenges the idea that QGP-like behaviour requires heavy nuclei.
